object_description: Simple recessed building block integrated into a sloping urban site
design_condition: The building is placed in the southwest corner and set deeply into the slope, preserving the listed forecourt and creating appropriately scaled open spaces while appearing unusually recessed from the street.

positive.statement: The simple building fits well into the grain of the surrounding context.
The listed forecourt is respected and preserved, while the terrain difference is overcome by a restrained staircase.
The rooms are correctly arranged and well sized for the desired sports operation.
The space-efficient implementation of the required program is operationally robust and achieves very good construction economics.
The resource-saving timber construction with horizontal facade formwork is rated as sustainable.

negative.statement: The trough-like excavation required for the window band has a problematic overall effect.
The building conveys a closed and forbidding expression that is inappropriate for its exposed setting.
The open technical area on the roof is clearly visible from higher ground and is not convincing as a fifth facade.
The access areas lack space and a designated stay or arrival area, while a single access would simplify access control.
The sports hall can only be illuminated through roof skylights, and the multifunctional rooms have too little daylight.
The outdoor arrangement of the ventilation units is not optimal and makes maintenance and upkeep complex.
The missing photovoltaic system must be supplemented for the energy standard to be achieved.
The compactness leads to limited and unattractive access areas and leaves the location, program, and architectural potential insufficiently developed.
